newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada wholesale trade unchanged in July.
newsitem.headline: Canada wholesale trade unchanged in July.

text.p: Canada's wholesale trade, seasonally adjusted, remained virtually unchanged in July at C$21.12 billion, Statistics Canada said on Monday.
Inventories, adj C$31.33 bln +0.3 pct +1.2 pct
Note - dollar figures are billions. Other figures are percentage changes.
A Reuter survey of economists had forecast a 0.7 percent month-on-month rise in July. Statscan also revised its figure for June sales to C$21.11 billion from C$21.14 billion.

Statistics Canada said despite slower sales in June and July, growth in wholesale sales so far this year was comparable to the recoveries in 1993 and 1994 and in sharp contrast to the 3.6 percent decline in 1995, the agency said.

A strong U.S. economy, together with falling mortgage rates and rising housing starts, boosted sales of lumber and building materials. Wholesale sales of food products, industrial and other machinery, equipment and supplies also rose in July.

The gains were offset by declines in other products, as well as in apparel and dry goods. The "other products" category combines a large number of products, including agricultural chemicals and other farm supplies, forest products and livestock.
Wholesalers recorded a slight increase in inventories in July, the second rise since the beginning of the year. It was mostly due to higher inventories of other products and food products.
